title: Namibe May Day labor march reported by port company
location: Namibe Province; exact assembly site and route unknown.
organizer: Union of Namibe Syndicates (reported by Empresa Portuária do Namibe)
participants_original: Opened official port-company report says port employees joined a May Day march organized by the Union of Namibe Syndicates, under a slogan referring to decent work, fair wages and social justice. No numeric or qualitative crowd size is provided.
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown. S006 gives no attendance estimate; presence of employees, companies or a vice-governor cannot establish 50 participants.

title.summary: Official Empresa Portuária do Namibe page describes a May Day march organized by the Union of Namibe Syndicates.

start_date.summary: S006 is dated 1 May 2025 and describes the May Day march as taking place that day.

location.summary: The source identifies the Union of Namibe Syndicates and port-company participants; it does not specify an assembly address or route. Namibe Province is the supported administrative scope.

organizer.summary: Union of Namibe Syndicates is named as organizer.

demands.summary: Reported slogan refers to decent work, fair wages and social justice; coded labor_wage_dispute as a provisional thematic mapping. The recipient/state target is not explicit.

participants_original.summary: Qualitative report of port employees and other organizations, no numeric or minimum estimate.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No participant count or other evidence establishing at least 50.

state_response.summary: No state response to the march is reported. Vice-Governor attendance is not treated as accommodation or policy response.

eligibility.summary: Plausible public labor march with a stated wage/work-related grievance, but the body does not give attendance ≥50 or an explicit demand recipient. Retained as pending_state_target with threshold unresolved; not proposed for inclusion.

notes: This candidate reflects only the specific S006 body, not the separate Luanda May Day event reported by ELISAL or derivative/out-of-period DigiPress coverage. Keep attendance unbounded and state targeting unresolved. No official approval or baseline merge.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people assemble in Namibe?
Were the wage/decent-work demands directed to the Angolan government or its policy, employers, or another recipient?
What was the exact assembly site/route, physical end and any related event continuity?
Can an independent source verify the gathering and clarify whether it was a protest rather than a commemorative march?
